stories.headline: Clashes and fires break out as protesters rally across France, joining students
stories.deck: Police fired tear gas and water cannons to push back people wearing hoods and masks and throwing fireworks, paving stones and other objects at officers in the Place de la République, northeast of the Paris city centre
stories.bodyText:
Cars were set on fire and shops were looted in Paris on Saturday (October 17, 2026) as police used tear gas and water cannons to disperse violent protesters who joined nationwide demonstrations against rising living costs and in support of high school students' grievances.
Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez's office reported “a growing number of violent incidents” across the country, including assaults on officers, looting and damage to public buildings. Police made at least 272 arrests across the country, including in Paris.
Protesters across France responded to calls on social media to revive the “yellow vest” movement, which emerged in 2018 against social injustice. Demonstrators expressed widespread frustration and anger at the government as gasoline, energy and food prices have spiked in recent months.
Police fired tear gas and water cannons to push back people wearing hoods and masks and throwing fireworks, paving stones and other objects at officers in the Place de la République, northeast of the Paris city centre.
Associated Press reporters saw thick black smoke rising from cars, bicycles and other vehicles, and trash bins on fire. A kiosk was also burning, while several shops have been looted. Several people have been injured in the clashes.
Police tried to prevent other small groups of protesters from converging on government buildings, Mr. Nuñez's office said.
Many metro stations were closed on Saturday (October 17) at police request, including those around the Champs-Elysées and near the presidential palace, parliament, and government offices.
Meanwhile, the majority of peaceful protesters joined a march that moved toward northwestern Paris. The crowd chanted France's national anthem and waved flags, and some people played trumpets and violins.
Violence hits Lyon, Marseille, and other cities
In Lyon, France's third-largest city where about 20,000 protesters joined the march, a fire broke out inside a tourist office.
In the southern port city of Marseille, some shops and a municipal police station were damaged, while protesters briefly forced their way into the lobby of City Hall.
“This is unacceptable," Marseille Mayor Benoît Payan told BFM TV, describing the damage in City Hall as “limited.”
Mr. Nuñez's office also reported violence by masked groups in Rennes, Toulouse, Montpellier and Grenoble, among other cities.
Sonia Mabrouk, 40, said she came from a suburb west of Paris with her daughter, a high school student, to protest “everything that's going wrong,” particularly the neglect of public services. Ms. Mabrouk, who took part in the yellow vest protests, criticised “policies that favour the rich and always hit the poorest people in their wallets.”
Many protesters could be seen wearing the fluorescent yellow vests that became a symbol of the 2018 rallies. “There's a general sense of frustration and anger,” Ms. Mabrouk said, as she marched alongside peaceful demonstrators of all ages.
Saturday's (October 17) protests follow weeks of school blockades
Student groups protesting since mid-September through school blockades have urged supporters to join them.
The CGT, one of France's major labour unions, also backed the protests, calling for “higher wages and pensions, lower prices and the protection of public services that meet people's needs.”
It said that over 500,000 protesters joined the rallies on Saturday (October 17).
In recent weeks, France has seen thousands of arrests, hundreds of injuries and schools set on fire as the new school year descended into nationwide student protests that are influencing the country's presidential election campaign and drawing international attention.
Far-left presidential candidate Jean-Luc Mélenchon, who backed high school students movement, also took part in the Paris protest on Saturday (October 17).
Among protesters, particularly gruesome wounds suffered by some teenagers have been blamed on police riot-control weapons. Mr. Nuñez suspended the use of a type of police stun grenade against the young demonstrators after a 15-year-old lost a hand.

stories.headline: INS Samarthak, first indigenous multi-purpose vessel, commissioned
stories.deck: Vice-President C.P. Radhakrishnan presided over the commissioning in Karwar of the first of two multi-purpose vessels built by Larsen & Toubro, with over 75% indigenous content, designed to test indigenously developed sensors and weapons
stories.bodyText:
The Indian Navy on Friday (October 16, 2026) commissioned INS Samarthak, the first of two multi-purpose vessels being built by Larsen & Toubro (L&T), strengthening its capability to test and evaluate indigenously developed sensors and weapons amid an evolving maritime security environment.
Vice-President C.P. Radhakrishnan presided over the commissioning ceremony in the presence of Chief of the Naval Staff Admiral Krishna Swaminathan, the Karnataka Governor, and senior naval and defence officials in Karwar.
According to the Indian Navy, designed and constructed by L&T Shipyard, INS Samarthak marks a significant milestone in India’s indigenous shipbuilding efforts, highlighting the growing role of the private sector in developing platforms for the armed forces. The vessel has over 75% indigenous content, according to the Navy.
Conceived primarily as a versatile platform for trials and evaluation, the ship will support the testing and training of new sensors and weapons developed by domestic industry. Its induction is expected to strengthen the Navy’s ability to validate indigenous technologies before their wider operational deployment, it added.
The vessel incorporates modular construction and pre-outfitting techniques aimed at optimising the shipbuilding process and reducing construction timelines. The project has also contributed to employment generation and the development of domestic industrial capabilities.
Named Samarthak, meaning ‘the proponent’, the vessel has been designed to undertake a range of operational and developmental tasks. Besides supporting trials and evaluation, it can carry out maritime surveillance and reconnaissance, offshore patrolling and humanitarian assistance and disaster relief operations.
The Navy said the vessel’s versatility would be particularly useful in an unpredictable maritime environment, where traditional security challenges are increasingly accompanied by non-traditional threats.
The commissioning also underscores the growing partnership between the Navy and India’s domestic shipbuilding industry as the government pursues self-reliance in defence manufacturing. The vessel is expected to provide a dedicated platform for testing indigenous systems, helping reduce dependence on foreign facilities for the evaluation of naval technologies.
The induction of INS Samarthak is part of the Navy’s broader effort to strengthen its operational capabilities while supporting the development of a resilient domestic defence industrial ecosystem.

stories.headline: FSSAI cracks down on Priyagold biscuit maker
stories.bodyText:
The FSSAI has taken legal action against three companies over serious violations of food safety standards
NEW DELHI: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has stepped up enforcement against major food companies, sanctioning prosecution against Priyagold biscuit maker Surya Food & Agro Ltd, Dodla Dairy Ltd and Ueir Organic Foods Pvt Ltd, while issuing notices to Nestlé India and Hindustan Unilever (HUL) over alleged labelling violations and misleading product claims.
Online listings described them as “Coffee Flavoured Milk” and carried claims about the goodness of flavoured double-toned milk, which FSSAI said were inconsistent with the declared product category. The companies have been asked to explain why action should not be initiated under food safety laws.
We will be submitting our response to the authorities and will be engaging with them as per due process established under law.” Hindustan Unilever was issued notices over claims on Horlicks Women’s Plus Chocolate Nutrition Drink, including “Nutrition for Strong Bones” and “Clinically Proven to Help Improve Bone Strength in 6 Months”.
Anuja Jaiswal is a Senior Assistant Editor at The Times of India, with an impressive 18-year career in narrative journalism. She specializes in health and heritage reporting, expertly simplifying complex health information to make it engaging and understandable for readers. Her deep dives into heritage topics are well-researched, resulting in captivating narratives that resonate with her audience. Over the years, she has worked in Chandigarh, Chhattisgarh and West UP, gaining diverse on-ground experience that shapes her storytelling.

stories.headline: Kolkata Durga Puja stampede: Police detain 12, including organisers
stories.bodyText: Kolkata: Police on Saturday night detained 12 people, including organisers of the Chorebagan Durga Puja in connection with their probe into the stampede in which 19 people died and 24 were injured, an officer said. . The move came after West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari promised strict action against those who failed to carry out their respective duties that allegedly led to the crowd mismanagement in the north Kolkata Durga Puja. . "We have detained 12 people in connection with our probe into the Chorebagan incident. Our officers are talking to them to find out the cause that led to today's mishap. If any lapses are found, we will act as per the law," the officer told PTI. .West Bengal CM forms high-level panel to review safety at Durga Puja pandals after 19 die at Chorbagan stampede. The stampede happened at the Chorebagan Durga Puja pandal in north Kolkata following a crowd surge amid rain on Saturday evening, the day of Maha Saptami. . Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari earlier said, "An SIT headed by a sitting judge of the Calcutta High Court will investigate the incident. The SIT will comprise members from STF, CID and other departments." . Anti-Rowdy Section (ARS) of Kolkata Police has collected CCTV footage of that place during the mishap. . "We will check the footage and take appropriate measures against those who failed to manage the crowd. That could be a member of the puja committee, a homeguard, a temporary worker, a policeman, or a private company security guard. Nobody will be spared," Adhikari said.

briefs.headline: Gruha Jyothi survey: Bescom asks owners of locked, vacant houses to submit documents by Oct. 31
briefs.bodyText:
After extending the deadline for the Gruha Jyothi door-to-door survey to October 31, Bangalore Electricity Supply Company Limited (Bescom) has asked consumers who could not be covered during the ongoing survey, particularly those whose houses were found locked or vacant, to visit their nearest Bescom sub-division office and submit the required documents.
On Thursday (October 15, 2026), Bescom said in a release that the move was aimed at ensuring that all eligible beneficiaries are covered under the scheme and that none are left out of the survey.
During the survey, Bescom identified 16.09 lakh locked houses and 28,519 vacant houses where no one was available to furnish the documents required for the survey.
The release also stated that this is the final, one-time opportunity for beneficiaries to verify their documents, and that the Energy Department will not undertake the exercise again.

briefs.headline: Trump waives sanction threat over Russian oil purchases
briefs.deck: Move offers relief to Indian refiners amid West Asia conflict; decision comes ahead of U.S. midterm elections
briefs.bodyText:
U.S. President Donald Trump on Saturday (October 17, 2026) waived key provisions of a new law that authorised punitive tariffs on countries purchasing Russian oil, offering relief to India.
The ‘Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026’ (SRIA Act), ratified on September 18, authorised increasing tariffs on countries continuing to buy Russian oil by as much as 100% as Washington sought to tighten Moscow’s oil revenues.
The waiver announced on Saturday (October 17, 2026) assures Indian refiners of greater flexibility to continue to purchase oil from Moscow, with supplies from West Asia affected because of the resurgence of conflict.
Ahead of trade talks
The decision by Mr. Trump that comes just ahead of the October 18 deadline set by the Congress for a determination on sanctions is also expected to ease the discussions during U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio’s visit to Mumbai and Jamnagar from October 20 to 22, when he will meet External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar.
Asked whether Mr. Jaishankar would discuss the sanctions or the diesel deal with Mr. Rubio, Foreign Ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said on Friday (October 16) that energy would be on the agenda. India had “always advocated for stability in global energy markets”, he said.
‘Helpful for India’
The Ministry of External Affairs had not responded to a request for comment on the Trump administration’s decision at the time of the filing, though an official termed the development “helpful” for India.
The official said that after the SRIA Act was ratified in September, the Indian government had taken a tougher stance than it did in the past. It conveyed to Washington the “implications” of imposing sanctions on India’s purchases of Russian oil.
Days after the legislation was signed into law, Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman had also said that India could not stop buying Russian oil, as doing so could raise global oil prices and alternative sources were limited amid the conflict in the Gulf.
The oil basket conundrum
Russian crude accounted for more than 50% of India’s oil imports in July, though it fell to 44% in August, with more volumes coming in from the UAE and the U.S.
Moscow’s share declined further to about 35% in September, according to data from real-time analytics provider Kpler.
Other than India, China is among the top purchasers of Russian oil — accounting for about 30% of its import basket.
The availability of Russian oil — now without any threat of sanctions — could ease the supply situation in the global oil market, which has been facing a crunch because of the resurgence in conflict in West Asia.
Benchmark Brent crude futures closed 0.8% higher at $109.95 a barrel on Friday (October 16).
Moreover, the Organisation of the Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) earlier this week also lowered its forecast for growth in global oil demand in 2026 by 0.2 million barrels per day (md/b) from 0.4 mb/d it estimated a month earlier.
U.S. midterms a priority
An early indication of Washington’s decision came this week with Mr. Trump’s announcement of a diesel deal with Russia, indicating that rising prices in the U.S. were now a bigger priority than punishing Russia and countries like India for energy trade.
Prices of diesel and gasoline in the U.S. surged in the recent past, more importantly, ahead of the midterm elections.
In fact, the Paris-headquartered International Energy Agency (IEA) has also indicated that continued disruptions to diesel exports from West Asia, compounded by lower supply from Russia and some Asian countries, have reduced global availability by 1.5 million barrels per day in the second half of the calendar year.
Published - October 17, 2026 07:30 am IST

briefs.headline: Census 2027: The pressures of counting India
briefs.deck: Enumerators working on the Census are facing several challenges in the field, including heat, connectivity issues, and safety concerns. Though the exercise is being conducted through a digital system designed for real-time monitoring, field workers say conditions on the ground and supervisory instructions are affecting data collection. Vijaita Singh reports on the challenges
briefs.bodyText:
Every day for about a month, M. Soumina, a government-school teacher, began her mornings by knocking on the doors of apartments in a multi-storey residential complex in East Delhi’s Mayur Vihar.
Although the school where she taught was closed for the summer break, Soumina had her task cut out for her after being appointed an enumerator for the ongoing Census. The exercise relies on about 33 lakh government teachers and other enumerators, who will spend nearly a year surveying an estimated 1.4 billion Indians on housing, amenities, and demographics.
For Soumina, the work meant spending hours going door to door in a brutal Delhi summer, with temperatures consistently hovering between 40°C and 42°C. She surveyed 150 flats spread across 17 apartment blocks and administered a 33-question survey to each household within 26 days.
“I was making those visits daily from May 19,” said Soumina. “I had an app on my phone to record the data. Before asking the questions, the households also have to be mapped and geotagged on the app.”
Other than her smartphone, a black bag, a QR-enabled identity card, and a white cap with the Census logo to protect her from the heat, Soumina’s companion during these visits was her husband, who works in the production unit of a newspaper. She said she felt safer with him around.
Like Soumina, enumerators working on the Census report facing several challenges in the field, including heat, connectivity issues, and safety concerns. Though the exercise is being conducted through a digital system designed for real-time monitoring, field workers said conditions on the ground and supervisory instructions are affecting data collection. Many of them have also flagged these issues on social media.
A massive exercise
The questions that enumerators asked are part of the Houselisting and Housing Operations (HLO), the first phase of the Population Census 2027. The questionnaire was notified by the Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India on January 22.
The 2027 Census marks several firsts: it is India’s first fully digital Census, the first to collect caste data, and the first to allow residents to self-enumerate. The exercise was originally scheduled for 2021, but was postponed because of the COVID-19 pandemic. As a result, India is conducting its population count six years later than the decennial schedule, with governments continuing to rely on 2011 Census data for policy planning and welfare programmes.
The HLO phase involves the collection of data on housing conditions, household composition, basic amenities, and assets to assess living standards. It captures information on the structure of dwellings; access to water, sanitation, and energy, ownership of consumer goods, and the number of people living in a household. It also collects residents’ mobile numbers for official communication.
The HLO phase will lay the foundation for the second phase of the Census — Population Enumeration — scheduled for February 2027. In Ladakh and the snow-bound regions of Uttarakhand, Jammu and Kashmir, and Himachal Pradesh, both phases have been set a deadline of September 30, 2026, due to weather constraints.
The second phase will enumerate caste and collect other detailed individual-level data, including religion. Each enumerator gets an honorarium of ₹25,000 for completing the task. So far, 23 States and Union Territories have completed the first phase.
Meeting strangers
With several occupants being working professionals, Soumina said it was difficult to get them to answer questions during the day.
“Most residents leave for work around 8.30 in the morning. So I visited homes between 7 and 7.30 with my husband. While some were accommodative, others asked us to come again later or skip the exercise altogether,” she said.
If a house was locked, she would go back again and again until she got the data, Soumina added. “Sometimes the visit extended into the evening, so I would again go with my husband.”
Like her, many female enumerators, mostly government school teachers, said they asked their husbands or other male members in their families to accompany them during field visits.
Meenu Verma, a primary school teacher from Rae Bareli, Uttar Pradesh, said that her husband and brother-in-law helped her during the exercise. “I was assigned 172 houses,” she said. “My husband and I used to wake up at 4 in the morning and reach the assigned village by 7. From 7 to about 11, we would find people in their homes, but after noon, due to the heat, the entire village would be deserted.”
She said they would then hesitate to knock on doors. “Many of them had no awareness about the Census, so we had to first explain it them. I want to request the government to appoint enumerators in pairs. Or a male colleague should accompany a female enumerator. Not everyone is polite. And in villages, houses are spread afar,” Verma said.
On May 21, a First Information Report (FIR) was registered against a Delhi resident for allegedly harassing a female Census enumerator while she was on duty. On June 13, a Delhi court convicted the accused, Sandeep Panwar, 43, for the crime. Earlier, on April 25, a female Census enumerator was allegedly denied entry into an apartment building in Bengaluru where an unidentified individual allegedly used abusive language against her, following which an FIR was registered against him.
Dinesh Kumar Dwivedi, a Hindi lecturer at a government school, who was Soumina’s supervisor, said six enumerators were reporting to him. “Fetching data from slum clusters was easier than seeking information from multi-storey apartments,” he said.
In Haryana and Delhi, Census enumerators, mostly government school teachers, complained that they faced hostility and were denied entry by residents of high-rise buildings and residents’ welfare associations (RWAs). The district administration of Gurugram wrote letters to RWAs saying that according to Section 8(2) of the Census Act, 1948, every resident is “legally bound” to answer Census-related questions to the best of their knowledge or belief.
“The slum residents were hesitant initially,” said Dwivedi, who collected data as an enumerator during the 2011 Census. “They thought this was an exercise to demolish the slums. When they understood its purpose, they were more than forthcoming. Some thought that participating in it would make them eligible for government schemes. Many others came to us with documents, asking for help in applying for welfare schemes.”
Dwivedi recalled that in 2011, the process was tedious: all the data had to be noted down on paper, which could get lost or damaged. He said residents were reluctant to share information on assets as they feared tax raids.
The digital divide
Beyond personal safety, the digital divide in India has also affected fieldwork. In metros and towns with better mobile connectivity, enumerators entered data directly on their phones. Elsewhere, they said they recorded details on paper or in notebooks and uploaded them on the app after going back home.
According to the Comprehensive Modular Survey: Telecom, conducted from January to March 2025 as a part of the 80th round of the National Sample Survey, 83.3 % of rural households and 91.6% of urban households had access to Internet. The total number of households surveyed was 34,950 (19,071 in rural areas and 15,879 in urban areas) and the total number of people was 1.42 lakh (82,573 in rural areas and 59,492 in urban areas). In the survey, a person was considered to have “used the internet” if they had accessed it at least once in the past three months.
“Connectivity is a huge issue, especially in rural areas. Once an enumerator has logged in, it is difficult to make changes, and if the network is poor, the data can get corrupted,” said an enumerator from U.P.
Enumerators use their own phones to collect the data and have been asked not to delete the apps during the enumeration phase. However, they said the app crashes often.
On the Google Play Store, the Census 2027 Houselist App, which has more than 10 lakh downloads, has a rating of 2.9. It can only be downloaded by authorised users — enumerators, supervisors, and charge officers. Of the 4,570 reviews submitted, 2,054 users gave it a one-star rating, while 1,735 rated it five stars.
Facing FIRs
On the outskirts of Delhi, in U.P.’s Noida, Sector-6, Indu Prakash Singh, charge officer, who oversees the work of enumerators and supervisors, set up a camp office at the Indira Gandhi Cultural Centre to monitor Census-related work. Officials with technical expertise were stationed in a large hall, with computer screens placed on desks arranged in a semicircle.
Singh’s job was to ensure the smooth conduct of the exercise, which entailed surveying 2,309 house-listing blocks (HLBs), each comprising 150-180 households with a population of 800-1,000. The exercise ran from May 22 to June 20 in U.P.
Though Census activities are usually carried out by government employees, in U.P., private-school teachers were also enrolled to tide over the shortage of government school teachers.
“The district administration in Noida issued directions to engage teachers from private schools for Census work,” Singh said.
“But some of them moved the Allahabad High Court, which ruled in their favour, and 50% of the 1,000 teachers who were trained backed out at the last moment. We were forced to engage NGOs and other private people for the task,” said a government official in Noida.
In Maharashtra, over 500 private unaided and minority schools moved the Bombay High Court in May against notices, appointment orders, and coercive steps such as FIRs issued against their teaching and non-teaching staff for failing to report for Census duties.
On May 22, the Court granted interim protection to the school associations and observed that Section 4A of the Census Act applies only to “local authorities” and prima facie the Census Act and the Census Rules, 1990 do not impose any statutory obligation on private unaided schools to provide their staff as enumerators or supervisors.
There have been several instances of enumerators facing FIRs for not taking up the assigned work. Though the total figures are difficult to assess, at least two FIRs were filed in Haryana against 10 enumerators, while a case each was filed in Noida and Greater Noida against more than 80 enumerators on June 3.
The National Crime Records Bureau reports for 2010 and 2011, when the first and second phases of the Census were last conducted, do not mention any cases registered under the Census Act.
Enumerators took to social media to flag issues such as heat and connectivity problems. They also reported witnessing stark income inequality, and described pressure from superiors to edit data in the name of correcting discrepancies.
Editing data
Earlier, it often took months or even years to process Census forms. Mobile apps have now enabled real-time data monitoring through the Census Management and Monitoring System (CMMS) portal. Access to the data entered via the app is available not only to enumerators, but also to supervisors and charge officers. Enumerators said they were asked to change data, particularly for questions related to sanitation, electricity, and LPG connection.
A school teacher in Delhi said during training, for a question relating to “access to latrine”, they were asked not to select the “no” option. This is used as a category for households without access to a latrine, and indicates open defecation. The “Yes” option is further broken down into “Exclusively for household use only (1),” “Shared with other households (2),” and “Public latrine (3).”
“During training, we were told to fill in the data observed by us,” said an enumerator from Rajasthan. “On the field, many residents in my enumeration block said they defecate in the open. When I submitted the data, I was asked by my supervisor to revisit the homes and revise the data to show that the households had access to a latrine, even if a public toilet was anywhere in the vicinity.”
Another enumerator from U.P. said they were also asked to edit data on the main source of drinking water. The options include tap water from treated source/untreated source, well, hand pump, tubewell/borehole, spring, river/canal, tank/pond/lake, packaged/bottled water and other sources. Under the Jal Jeevan Mission, one of the flagship schemes of the Bharatiya Janata Party government, nearly 81.97% households in India have tap water connection.
“When I filled untreated tap water as an option, the supervisor and the charge officers asked me to change the entry to tap water from treated source. What is the point of door-to-door enumeration then,” asked the enumerator.
The question on the availability of a kitchen and LPG/PNG connection were also edited, the enumerator added. “Even if the house has an LPG connection in their name, they were using cow dung cakes or wooden logs to cook as they had not refilled the cylinders for several months. If we mentioned firewood or charcoal as the response, which is what we observed, we were asked to change the entry to show that the main fuel is LPG,” said an enumerator from Rajasthan. According to the Press Information Bureau, national LPG coverage rose from 55.9% in April 2014 to 107.2% in April 2026. Consumers grew from 14.51 crore to 33.39 crore in the same period.
On June 2, the Director of Census Operations, Rajasthan, wrote to all district functionaries saying “during the analysis of field data collected so far, some discrepancies have been noticed”. Charge officers were instructed to “verify the block-level data through the CMMS portal, in accordance with the actual field situation.”
Around 11 a.m. on June 12, Manish Kumar, a government employee, went to a building in Noida’s Sector-2. An open drain flowed on the side. Several doors were locked since many of the occupants, largely migrants, were away at work. In the courtyard of the three-storey building, a woman was washing bedsheets in a corner using two tubs of water. A man was taking a bath in a narrow veranda outside his one-room accommodation, which he shared with six other members of the family.
Kumar knocked on each door to ensure that every household was enumerated. The rooms that were open mostly had women and children inside. While some residents responded immediately, others were suspicious of Kumar. He noted down the details, stepped out of the building, and then logged the information into the Census app on his phone.
He said he would return in the evening and over the weekend to reach residents whose doors were locked. “A household must be labelled vacant or locked only after multiple visits,” he said.
Published - June 20, 2026 05:40 am IST

briefs.headline: Meerut woman, lover sentenced to death for killing her husband and leaving snake on his bed as cover-up
briefs.deck: Post-mortem examination found injury marks on his neck and nose and that he died of strangulation, police said
briefs.bodyText:
A court in Meerut on Friday (October 16, 2026) sentenced a woman and her lover to death for killing her husband and leaving a live snake beside his body to make it look like a case of snakebite, officials said.
Additional District and Sessions Judge Jaiveer Singh Nagar awarded the death penalty to Ravita and Amardeep for the murder of Amit Kashyap alias Mikky Kashyap, a resident of Akbarpur Sadat village in Meerut, the court officials said.
Amit was found dead on a cot in his house on April 13 last year and a live snake was found beside his body. His family initially suspected that he died due to a snakebite.
However, the post-mortem examination found injury marks on his neck and nose and that he died of strangulation, police said.
Published - October 16, 2026 04:35 pm IST

briefs.headline: Supreme Court agrees to list plea alleging Rahul Gandhi ‘pushed’ pregnant journalist during Oct. 12 march
briefs.deck: Orally mentioning the application before Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, senior advocate Gaurav Bhatia said the woman journalist was manhandled on the court premises
briefs.bodyText:
The Supreme Court on Friday (October 16, 2026) agreed to list an application alleging that Congress leader Rahul Gandhi pushed a pregnant journalist during a march to the apex court on October 12.
Orally mentioning the application before Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, senior advocate Gaurav Bhatia said the woman journalist was manhandled on the court premises.
Also Read: CJP Tiranga protest on October 16 2026
On October 12, Mr. Gandhi led a march to the Supreme Court, where he and a few Opposition bloc leaders reached the Supreme Court Registry as petitioners. They sought an independent probe into allegations of arbitrary use of power by Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and demanded the suspension of the Special Intensive Revision process. The court premises were teeming with lawyers and journalists, while Supreme Court security stopped a large crowd outside.
Mr. Bhatia submitted on Friday that the woman journalist was three months’ pregnant and had to be hospitalised.
The senior advocate had raised the same allegation against Mr. Gandhi in an apex court hearing held on Thursday (October 15). Mr. Bhatia represented a petition accusing the Congress leader of leading a “political procession” into the Supreme Court to “browbeat” the judiciary. The petition sought criminal contempt action against Mr. Gandhi and other Opposition leaders.
While making clear that “no one can browbeat the judiciary”, the Bench of Chief Justice Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi had issued notice on that petition.
On Friday, the Chief Justice said the application about the alleged conduct of Mr. Gandhi towards the woman journalist may be heard either on October 26 or the next day.
The court is closed for Dussehra throughout next week.
Published - October 16, 2026 02:03 pm IST

briefs.headline: Actor Imran Khan moves Bombay HC against ‘arbitrary, illegal’ notice to leave India
briefs.deck: Notice followed politically motivated complaint, led to violation of Sections 14 and 21 of the Constitution, says the actor in his writ petition; fresh notice asks the U.S. citizen to explain why his OCI card should not be cancelled
briefs.bodyText:
Terming the ‘leave India notice’ issued to him by the Foreigners Regional Registration Office (FRRO) in Mumbai as arbitrary, illegal, and unconstitutional, actor Imran Khan on Saturday (October 17, 2026) moved the Bombay High Court seeking its quash. The actor’s legal team, led by advocate Zulfikar Memon, is likely to mention the matter in the Bombay High Court on Monday (October 19, 2026).
Meanwhile, the FRRO on Saturday issued another notice to the actor, a U.S. citizen who has an Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) card, asking him to explain why his OCI card should not be cancelled. Mr. Khan has been given 15 days to respond. The earlier notice issued had asked the actor to leave the country before October 28.
In his writ petition filed on Saturday, Mr. Khan said that the notice had led to the violation of Sections 14 and 21 of the Constitution. He claimed that the action against him followed a politically motivated complaint registered by the leader of political party and asked why due process was not followed in the matter, questioning how the principles of natural justice can be overlooked.
The actor has also sought to know the basis on which the notice was issued. “The LIN [leave India notice] directs the petitioner to leave India by 28.10.2026 without disclosing any reasons, supporting material, or specific statutory contravention. It was issued without inquiry, a show-cause notice, or any opportunity for the petitioner to respond to the alleged violations,” the writ petition stated, alleging that a brief detention of Mr. Khan by the police on October 10 was “unjust.”
On October 10, Mr. Khan participated in a protest held in Mumbai seeking the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. The actor claimed that he was being arbitrarily targeted as a public figure and said that the notice itself did not cite any specific breach.
Mr. Khan has averred that the notice issued to him reflected “patent non-application of mind.” “Not only is the LIN manifestly disproportionate, if implemented, it would reduce the very principles of natural justice that the Respondents are duty bound to uphold to nothing but a dead letter,” the petition stated.
Mr. Khan said that he had not breached any provisions of the Immigration and Foreigners Act or the Citizenship Act. “No gathering was taking place when the petitioner arrived; he neither entered any restricted or barricaded area nor disobeyed the police direction to leave; and he was apprehended only after the media surrounded him while he was returning to his nearby vehicle,” the petition stated.
He said he had resided peacefully in India since the age of two years. “He has deep-rooted familial, marital, educational, and professional ties to the country, and has no criminal antecedents,” the petition said.

briefs.headline: Directorate General of Maritime Administration bans deployment of Indian seafarers in Malaysia’s Sarawak region
briefs.deck: Decision follows recurring fatal accidents of young Indian seafarers over the years
briefs.bodyText:
Expressing concern over recurring fatal accidents involving young Indian seafarers, the Directorate General of Maritime Administration (DGMA) has banned the recruitment or engagement of Indian seafarers in the Sarawak region of Malaysia.
The shipping regulator directed Recruitment and Placement Service Licence (RPSL) companies not to employ Indian seafarers for Inland, Riverline and Coastal Vessels of the Sarawak region saying that fatal accidents involving young Indian seafarers deployed in Malaysia had occurred on a recurring basis, year after year.
As part of the bilateral engagement between India and Malaysia on matters concerning the safety and regulation of Indian seafarers, the Malaysia Marine Department (MMD) had furnished findings and recommended preventive measures governing the recruitment, deployment, sign-on and sign-off of Indian seafarers on Malaysian-flagged vessels, to reduce fatalities.
Invoking provisions under Section 301 of the Merchant Shipping Act, 2025, the DGMA asked RPSL agencies not to deploy Indian seafarers on any vessel operating exclusively within the inland, riverine, coastal or port-limit waters of the Sarawak region of Malaysia.
₹1 crore insurance cover
In a related development, the DGMA told RPSL agencies to ensure mandatory insurance for Indian seafarers engaged in foreign flagged vessels. The norm would apply to vessels that were not covered under the Protection & Indemnity (P&I) insurance. In cases where a vessel was not covered under the P&I insurance, the RPSL agency should ensure that mandatory insurance coverage of not less than ₹1 crore per seafarer was obtained from any of the Insurance Regulatory Development Authority (IRDA) approved Indian insurance companies.
There was need for such an insurance to safeguard the dignity, safety and welfare of Indian seafarers and to ensure availability of valid and verifiable financial security in respect of vessels engaging Indian seafarers, the DGMA said.

Mr. John said the proposal was not intended to impose a financial obligation on local bodies or encroach upon their existing rights.
According to him, corporations and municipalities which had comparatively robust revenue bases than grama panchayats could choose to contribute to improving local KSRTC depots if they considered it necessary.

Around Nrupathunga Road, traffic was affected by Union Minister H.D. Kumaraswamy’s visit to the Director General of Police headquarters. Further, the police had made arrangements around J.C. Outstation buses

Keerthana M., a Koramangala resident who was travelling to her hometown of Hassan, said the bus she was travelling in was stuck within the city for almost two hours, and the journey to her district took six hours. “I took the bus around 3 p.m., thinking I would get out in the evening traffic but couldn’t escape,” she said.

Railway stations

stories.headline: Rs 100 per km, yet no guarantee of a ride in rain & traffic in Bengaluru
stories.bodyText:
Bengaluru:
 Rs 100 per kilometre or more was the price commuters were effectively paying for an AC cab in Bengaluru as 
rain
, traffic congestion and surge pricing drove up fares during the ongoing long weekend. With cabs hard to find, many commuters were left waiting for rides, dealing with frequent cancellations or opting for more expensive alternatives.
A reality check by 
TOI on major cab aggregator apps Saturday evening showed that a short, roughly 2-km ride from Residency Road to Church Street cost Rs 221 for an AC cab and Rs 202 for a non-AC cab on 
Uber
. An autorickshaw ride was priced at Rs 105.
Rapido quoted Rs 272 for an AC cab, Rs 255 for a non-AC cab and Rs 96 for an autorickshaw. Namma Yatri was relatively cheaper, with an AC cab costing Rs 200, a non-AC cab Rs 196 and an autorickshaw Rs 66 for the same journey.
On both Friday and Saturday, premium or priority options for AC cabs and autorickshaws cost at least Rs 30-40 more than the fares quoted for regular options. The higher fares did not necessarily guarantee a quicker ride. Waiting times were at least six to 10 minutes in most cases. Frequent cancellations added to the commuters’ woes.
Two major sporting events in the Central Business District (CBD) Saturday — the India-West Indies cricket match and the Bengaluru FC-Chennaiyin FC football match — added to the demand for cabs and to waiting times. Rain that began in the evening also affected cab availability in other parts of the city.
“I had to travel from Tumakuru Road to Seshadripuram when it started raining. I checked two apps, and Uber’s AC cab fare was almost Rs 100 more than Rapido’s. However, I couldn’t get a ride on either app even after adding boosters. A trip that would normally cost around Rs 250 was priced at Rs 377 on Uber and Rs 288 on Rapido,” said a commuter, Sparsha NM.
The surge in fares was evident Friday evening as well, when many residents were preparing to leave the city for the long weekend. The steep fares were not limited to the CBD. Commuters in other neighbourhoods also reported paying nearly twice their usual fares.
“I took a cab from Jayanagar Friday evening for a trip that would normally cost me Rs 150-160. This time, I paid almost Rs 300 — double my usual fare. With cab prices so high, I was forced to take an autorickshaw in the rain,” said commuter Sriharsha M.
Rides longer than 15km were costing at least Rs 750 – Rs 1,000, depending on the vehicle being booked on both days.
TOI reached out to Uber, Rapido and Namma Yatri, but they were unavailable for comment.

briefs.headline: Karnataka Health Minister urges public to use alternatives as 108 ambulance workers threaten strike from October 14 night
briefs.deck: Only 350-400 of 750 required ambulances operational; union seeks pay revision, adequate staffing and safety measures
briefs.bodyText:
With 108 ambulance service employees threatening to go on strike from Wednesday night (October 14, 2026), Health Minister U.T. Khader on Tuesday urged the public not to depend solely on the service over the next two months, citing a shortage of operational vehicles and delays in emergency response.
Against a requirement of around 750 ambulances across Karnataka, only 350 to 400 are currently operational, resulting in delays of 45 minutes to an hour in some cases, Mr. Khader said. He advised people to use ambulances available at government hospitals at the taluk level during emergencies.
New fleet by December
The government needs time until December to restructure the service and introduce a new fleet through a fresh tender process, he said. The existing fleet had deteriorated since 2018, making a revamp necessary.
“We have requested time until December to completely restructure the system,” Mr. Khader said, pointing out that the government was preparing a new tender policy to bring in ambulances under improved conditions.
Responding to the strike threat, the Minister said the government would not yield to pressure from the agency operating the service or its employees. He clarified that the staff were employees of GVK EMRI, the service operator, and not government employees. “If anything goes wrong or patients are affected, we will take action against GVK EMRI,” he said.
Demand of ambulance staff
The 108 Ambulance Workers’ Union has cited long-pending demands relating to wages, staffing and workplace safety. In a previous ultimatum, the union had warned of a service shutdown from 8 p.m. on September 22 if its demands were not met. The latest threat is for Wednesday night.
The union is seeking an annual salary increase and pay revision, a uniform pay structure across the State instead of zone-wise wages, and salaries linked to seniority. It has also demanded adequate ambulances to operate in three shifts, rest rooms for staff and changes to shift schedules.
Among its key demands is compensation of ₹50 lakh to the family of an employee killed in an accident while on duty. The union has said the demands have remained unresolved despite repeated appeals to the government.

briefs.headline: Bengaluru court restrains media, tech platforms from disseminating defamatory vidoes on Siddaramaiah

The interim order restrains 42 media houses, including newspapers, television channels, digital platforms like YouTube, Yahoo, Google and Facebook, from disseminating the impugned videos, their captions, clips, extracts, or substantially identical versions through any medium.
B. Pushpanjali, judge of the 19th additional city civil and sessions court, Bengaluru, passed the interim order on a suit filed by Mr. Siddaramaiah.
Additionally, the court directed YouTube, Yahoo, Google and Facebook, to forthwith disable access to and block the specified URLs of the two videos telecast on the YouTube channels on September 27, 2026, with title “Karnataka Honey Trap Nexus Part-1”, and October 2, 2026 with the title “Live: Biggest CD Blast in Karnataka Politics?”.
In the suit, Mr. Siddaramaiah categorically denied all the allegations made in the two videos. In one of the videos, a woman narrates a 2011 incident, allegedly when she was 14 and links it to him in a conversation with two men, “the recording of which was in a manner intended to resemble a clandestine or hidden-camera recording,” it has been stated in the suit.
The caption, it further says, “is deliberately framed to place the plaintiff at the centre of a sensational political and sexual narrative,” sans any material.
It has been pointed out in the suit that the caption to the video links the alleged recording of conversation as a reason for him to demit the office of Chief Minister, alleged blackmail, an alleged honey-trap network, the present Chief Minister, statements of other political leaders, the Congress High Command, and Leader of the Opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi.
“...The attempt to retrospectively connect a political transition with an alleged secretly recorded conversation is false, baseless and designed to injure Mr. Siddaramaiah’s reputation and political standing,” it has been claimed in the suit.
Since Mr. Siddaramaiah has challenged the authenticity, credibility, intent of the videos, the court observed that permitting their circulation at this stage could seriously harm his dignity, reputation and privacy. It noted that if media houses are not restrained from broadcasting or sharing the videos or their clips, the resulting damage would be irreparable.

briefs.headline: Karnataka to clear ₹100 crore in pending minority scholarships, says Minister

briefs.bodyText:
The Karnataka government will clear around ₹100 crore in pending minority scholarships, Minister for Minorities Welfare, Waqf and Haj U.T. Khader said on Tuesday, announcing measures to address students’ grievances and improve access to education.
The department plans to distribute ₹494.71 crore in scholarships and financial assistance to students from class 1 to PhD this year. The allocation is ₹440 crore, but the department is prepared to explore additional funding if applications exceed the available budget, he said.
Helpline
The department would also introduce an online helpline for students who have not received their scholarships or have complaints about the process.
Students could call 82777 99990 to register their grievances. The department would collect their details, track the cases and respond, Mr. Khader said. A ‘Minority Mitra’ mobile application is also planned in order to receive public complaints on matters handled by the department.
Skill training
The department was planning additional educational initiatives, including skill training to improve employment prospects, language laboratories and an artificial intelligence-based learning system to guide students according to their interests.
The department would also change the way NEET coaching is delivered to students in classes 9 and 10. Instead of relying only on online classes, teachers would visit schools to conduct offline coaching for a specified number of hours each week.
Shishunala Sharif schools
The department has also drawn up plans to establish new Shishunala Sharif schools after assessing local needs and accessibility for students.
The government plans to lay the foundation stone for 100 schools at an estimated cost of ₹800 crore by the end of November. Construction of 77 schools taken up earlier is in its final stages, and these are also expected to be inaugurated by the end of November, Mr. Khader said.
Extension of deadline
The State government has asked the Karnataka State Open University (KSOU) to extend the deadline for fee payment as thousands of students await reimbursement under a Minorities Welfare Department scheme, Minister U.T. Khader said.
More than 13,000 students applied for assistance this year, with the total fee requirement estimated at around ₹30 crore. The department has selected 8,086 students this year, compared with about 5,000 last year.
The scheme, introduced to help minority students pursue further education through correspondence courses, has run into financial constraints because the commitment extends beyond the first year of a course.
Over 5,000 applied last year
Last year, around 5,328 students applied, with the requirement estimated at ₹10 crore to ₹12 crore against an allocation of ₹5 crore. Additional funds were arranged to meet the shortfall. This year, the action plan provided ₹5 crore, even as applications rose sharply.
Mr. Khader said the government had requested KSOU to extend the fee-payment deadline and would work out the finances, subject to the necessary approvals. The university, which comes under the University Grants Commission, must also comply with its norms.
The department would frame clearer eligibility criteria, including the relevance of the postgraduate course to the student’s undergraduate qualification. Mr. Khader acknowledged that students had applied without being adequately informed about the budgetary limits and said the government would work towards a more sustainable system.

briefs.headline: Joint property owners in Bengaluru can now split A-eKhata online, get separate records
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru: In a move expected to benefit thousands of families and joint property owners in the city, Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA) and its five city corporations Saturday launched an online ‘plot sub-division’ service that allows owners holding a joint A-eKhata to split the property and obtain separate e-khatas.
The facility, introduced on the eAasthi 2.0 platform, addresses a long-pending demand from citizens who jointly own sites and often face difficulties while selling, gifting, mortgaging property, obtaining building plan approvals or paying property tax independently.
Under the new service, owners whose individual shares are clearly recorded in a single A-eKhata can apply online to divide the property and obtain separate A-eKhatas in their respective names. The provision applies to family members, legal heirs, relatives and even non-family joint owners.
Officials said the service will streamline property transactions and reduce dependence on manual processes. Once separate e-khatas are generated, each owner can independently manage property-related transactions, including sale, mortgage, gift deeds, building plan sanction and tax payments.
The facility is available only for A-eKhata properties where the ownership share of each joint holder is already recorded. 
It covers vacant sites and plots with buildings up to 2,000 sqm, while multi-storey apartment units are not eligible under this service. Larger plots exceeding 2,000 sqm must continue to follow the existing town planning approval process.
To qualify, every newly created plot must have a minimum area of 50 sqm, road frontage of at least six metres and independent access to a public road, either directly or through an internal road. Internal access roads, where required, must be at least 3.5 metres wide.
Applicants are required to upload a sub-division sketch prepared by a registered architect showing the original plot boundaries, the proposed division among owners and road access details.
The sub-division fee will be levied as a percentage of the property’s guidance value, ranging from 0.2% for residential properties to 0.5% for non-residential properties.
For instance, a residential property with a guidance value of Rs 1 crore would attract a fee of Rs 20,000.
The online application can be submitted through the GBA’s eAasthi portal, where owners can enter their details, upload documents and make payments digitally after approval.
—

Key features
-Joint A-eKhata holders can obtain separate e-khatas online
-Applicable to family and non-family joint owners
-Covers plots up to 2,000 sq m
-Fee ranges from 0.2% for residential properties to 0.5% for non-residential properties

stories.headline: Private banks’ profits rise, large lenders see margin pressure
stories.bodyText:
MUMBAI: Private sector banks reported higher profits in the Sept-quarter despite the top three banks seeing pressure on net interest margins (NIM).
The FCNR(B) deposits boosted the deposit growth rate to a decadal high and expanded balance sheets, but cost of deposits rose because of the higher rate being offered under the special scheme to NRIs.
The three largest private sector lenders by assets — 
HDFC Bank
, 
ICICI Bank
 and 
Axis Bank
 — reported margin compression in the second quarter as funding costs rose and deposit competition intensified. Axis Bank saw the sharpest decline, with NIM falling 37 basis points year on year (YoY) to 3.36% from 3.73%. Its net profit rose 37.6% to Rs 7,003 crore, supported by non-interest income and controlled credit costs.
ICICI Bank’s NIM fell 12 basis points to 4.18% from 4.3%, while net profit rose 20.1% to Rs 14,843 crore, aided by growth in advances. HDFC Bank’s margin declined 11 basis points to 3.16% from 3.27%, while net profit grew 4.7% to Rs 19,510 crore as it continued to adjust its credit-to-deposit ratio after merger with HDFC Ltd.
YES Bank reported a 65% YoY increase in net profit to Rs 1,080 crore for the quarter ended Sept 30, 2026, driven by higher net interest income and lower provisions. However, the bank said that if the Supreme Court order quashing the write-down of Rs 8,415 crore of AT-1 bonds had been factored in, it would have reported a loss of Rs 5,217 crore and net worth of Rs 46,970 crore, against the reported Rs 53,268 crore. 
Its NIM rose 10 basis points to 2.6% from 2.5%.
HDFC Bank’s margins also reflected the cost of raising $7 billion through FCNR(B) deposits at a weighted average landed cost of 6% to 6.25%, along with a higher share of non-retail assets and liabilities. The bank expects margins to recover over the coming quarters as lending rates reprice faster than funding costs, although rebalancing the asset mix will take two to three quarters. Its CASA ratio has weakened as households shift savings to higher-yielding instruments and the bank replaces maturing wholesale borrowings with bulk deposits. It has also chosen to concede mortgage market share rather than offer home loans at rates that would dilute profitability.
Some mid-sized private lenders and public sector banks recorded an expansion in NIM. Federal Bank’s margin rose 26 basis points to 3.32% from 3.06%, while net profit increased 45% to Rs 1,386 crore. Central Bank of India’s NIM expanded 12 basis points to 3.01% from 2.89%, supporting a 21% increase in net profit to Rs 1,469 crore. IDBI Bank recorded the largest margin expansion among the lenders in the comparison, with NIM rising 40 basis points to 4.11% from 3.71%. Its net profit, however, fell 39% to Rs 2,206 crore, reflecting higher provisions or a normalisation of non-core income against a high base.

Noel cast the shift as a return to the founders’ purpose. “Our founders did not set out to build the largest group of companies,” he wrote. “They believed that enterprise carried with it a responsibility to society, and that the true measure of progress was an improvement in the quality of people’s lives.”
Its earlier institutions include Indian Institute of Science in Bengaluru and Mumbai’s Tata Hospital.
Noel named education as a priority. India needed more institutions that nurture talent at home, he said, so students are not forced to look overseas. In healthcare, the Trusts are working towards a network of 40-50 not-for-profit general hospitals.

stories.headline: Robert E. Hall and Michael Woodford | Putting people in economics
stories.deck: The winners of the 2026 Economics Nobel Prize transformed macroeconomics by showing how individual choices, household expectations and business behaviour shape the economy and influence the effectiveness of government policies
stories.bodyText:
Most people view macroeconomics as a result of the mechanical tweaking of some variables to alter other variables. For example, if aggregate consumer demand is down, there is immediately a call for lower interest rates and higher government doles. Similarly, when demand outstrips supply, then the call is the opposite: raise interest rates and cut back on handouts.
There was also a long-held belief that unemployment and inflation had an inverse relationship — as shown in the famous Phillips Curve — and that income and consumption moved in tandem. If governments could tweak one, the belief was that this would result in changes in the other.
It was this that Robert E. Hall and Michael Woodford turned on its head, for which they were awarded the 2026 Sveriges Riksbank Prize in Economic Sciences in Memory of Alfred Nobel, commonly called the Economics Nobel. The economic thinking that the ‘invisible hand’ of the government should step in to stabilise the economy was born out of the landmark work of that titan of economic theory, John Maynard Keynes, and was put to great use in the aftermath of the Great Depression in the U.S. in the 1930s.
This stabilisation policy remained popular for several decades until it was upended by the oil shock the U.S. economy faced in the 1970s. During this crisis, the relationship between several macroeconomic variables broke down. That is, inflation rose at an accelerated pace even though unemployment was high, and the link between income and consumption looked like it was no longer holding.
What this meant was that conventional stabilisation policy no longer worked — government stimulus came at the wrong time, which had long-term detrimental effects on growth and inflation.
Economists such as Robert E. Lucas, the 1995 Economics Nobel Prize winner, then got to work to show that the dry mechanisms of simply working with macroeconomic variables were not the way. Inflation at the macro level was the result of pricing decisions by thousands of individual companies, and total private consumption was the result of actions taken by lakhs of individual households.
However, while it was increasingly accepted that households make consumption choices not only on the basis of their current situation but also on the basis of their future expectations, the difficulty arose in trying to quantify the effect of these future expectations.
Policy and behaviour
Enter Robert E. Hall. Born in 1943 in Palo Alto, California, Mr. Hall graduated from UC Berkeley in 1964 and earned his PhD from MIT. Even as a graduate student, he was already working on the issue of how government policy affects business behavior, research that eventually led to a seminal 1967 paper ‘Tax Policy and Investment Behavior’.
He went on to serve on the economics faculty of UC Berkeley from 1967 to 1970 before moving to MIT and then to Stanford University, where he still works as the Robert and Carole McNeil Joint Hoover Senior Fellow and Professor of Economics.
Mr. Hall’s greatest contribution, and for which he was awarded the Nobel Prize, however, had to do with the households not companies.
The central idea of his research, later put down in a landmark paper in 1978, was that if the consumption decisions of households is governed by their expectations of future income and other such factors, then their current consumption is also an accurate indicator of their future expectations. That is, if a household is optimistic about the future, it will consume more than if it were pessimistic.
A related observation was that households will also only ever change their consumption patterns if their assessment of the future changes. In turn, their assessment of the future changes when they obtain new and relevant information. Further, since new information cannot be predicted by definition, changes in consumption also cannot be predicted.
Now, here is the key for policymakers. If the rule is that changes in consumption cannot be predicted because they are based on unpredictable new information, then situations where it can be predicted must be because households are breaking this rule. This breaking of the rules usually takes place when a household is living paycheck to paycheck, or hand-to-mouth. They cannot borrow and have no savings, and so they spend only exactly what they earn. That is, their consumption is entirely predictable.
Using this finding, and the empirical work done by Mr. Hall, policymakers could now measure in exact terms the percentage of the population that was living hand-to-mouth.
The other major contribution of Mr. Hall’s work was bringing in a ‘human’ element to macroeconomics, providing policymakers a map of sorts to how individuals react to both fear and confidence about the future.
Mr. Hall’s work addressed the demand side, giving macroeconomics microeconomic underpinnings. The supply side theory was a result of the work done by Michael Woodford.
Mr. Woodford was born in 1955 in Massachusetts and he went on to complete his undergraduate studies at the University of Chicago, earn a Juris Doctor from Yale Law School, and complete his PhD in Economics from MIT. Not only did Mr. Woodford build on Mr. Hall’s demand side contributions, but he also brought about a decisive change in how inflation was viewed. That is, in a series of papers starting in the 1990s, he showed that inflation is based on the behaviour of individual companies that set prices, knowing that it would be too difficult to change these prices every time demand or input costs change. Firms are not only future-looking in their behaviour, but their prices also tend to be ‘sticky’ — they don’t change quickly.
Looking to the future
Now, the follow-up of this for policymakers was that, since businesses look to the future, their expectations about future interest rates are very important to manage inflation. As a result, it becomes of prime importance for central bank policies to be credible and transparent.
That is why the RBI Governor, while announcing interest rate decisions, puts them in the context of the global and Indian economies, and gives the rationale and outlook in detail. This policy of transparency is followed by all major central banks around the world and has its foundations in Mr. Woodford’s work.
Other aspects of Mr. Woodford’s work also provided policymakers more effective tools to deal with supply shocks than they had during the 1970s, such as using monetary policy to do the job rather than fiscal policy.
Mr. Woodford combined all of this with Mr. Hall’s demand side theory and created a complete framework, which he published in a 2003 monograph titled Making Things Happen: A Theory of Causal Explanation. This monograph laid the groundwork for understanding business cycles, what causes them, how they play out, their impact on stabilisation policy, and the importance of policy transparency.
In essence, the two economists provided the theoretical and empirical underpinnings to a basic but powerful idea for policymakers: the economy is made out of the people in it.

stories.headline: Air India sets up multi-disciplinary panel to identify cost-saving opportunities
stories.deck: The airline will also be launching 'PRABHAV - The Value Creator Award', an initiative to gather cost-reduction ideas from the staff, and those providing ideas that can be implemented will be rewarded.
stories.bodyText:
Loss-making Air India has set up a multi-disciplinary team to identify cost-saving opportunities, with the new CEO Tewolde Gebremariam urging the staff to embed a mindset of frugality and accountability in all their works.
Mr. Gebremariam, who officially took over the reins as CEO and MD on October 1, told the employees this week that every rupee saved creates an opportunity to reinvest in areas that matter the most, including operations and customer experience.
Also Read: Air India extends cancellation of Saudi Arabia flights till October 20
The airline will also be launching 'PRABHAV - The Value Creator Award', an initiative to gather cost-reduction ideas from the staff, and those providing ideas that can be implemented will be rewarded.
"A multidisciplinary, cross-functional Cost Savings Team has been established on full-time basis to identify cost-saving opportunities across the organisation," he said in a message to the staff on October 12.
The team will systematically review all expenditure and identify cost-saving opportunities across functions, he said and mentioned that the airline was navigating an exceptionally challenging operating environment.
"Ongoing airspace closures, the conflict in the Middle East and its resulting operational disruptions, and persistently high jet fuel costs continue to place significant pressure on airlines across the industry," he said.
Air India, which is jointly owned by Tata Group and Singapore Airlines, recorded a consolidated loss of Rs 22,238.23 crore for 2025-26 financial year.
According to Mr. Gebremariam, 'PRABHAV' will invite ideas from employees that reduce costs through smarter ways of working, improved utilisation, improved processes, contract optimisation and/or renegotiation, insourcing of outsourced activities and optimal use of resources.
Also, the ideas can be on cost effective and efficient procurement of goods and services and waste reduction, questioning the status quo or maximise revenue through new opportunities and deriving greater value from the existing products, services and capabilities, he added.
The airline has also made changes to the approval matrix for SOD (Staff On Duty).
From October 1, all approvals will now be routed through the HOD, CXO, and CEO, ensuring greater rigour, transparency, and alignment in decision-making across the organisation, Mr. Gebremariam said in the message.
Air India's consolidated loss widened to Rs 22,238.23 crore in the fiscal year ended March 2026 from Rs 10,858.83 crore a year ago amid multiple headwinds.
During the same period, total income declined to Rs 71,869.94 crore from Rs 78,635.61 crore, according to regulatory filings. The consolidated figures include financials of Air India Express.
Stressing the importance of being cost consciousness, the CEO said that alongside operational excellence, "we need to embed a mindset of frugality, accountability, and thoughtful decision-making in everything that they do".
"By embracing a culture of accountability, prudent spending, and operational excellence, each of us can play a meaningful role in shaping Air India's long-term success," he said.
He also said that cost savings cannot be driven by a single team and requires the active participation and commitment of every employee.
An Ethiopian Airlines veteran, Mr. Gebremariam is the second foreigner to head Air India, which was acquired by the Tata Group from the government in January 2022.

briefs.bodyText:

There is no change in the duty of either of the retail fuels meant for domestic consumption.
The export levy on petrol has been increased to ₹2.5 per litre from ₹0.5 per litre as accorded in the last review.
Diesel exports would now be subject to a levy of ₹8.5 per litre, lower than ₹16 per litre from the last review.
Levy on ATF remains unchanged at ₹10.5 per litre.
The rates are applicable for a fifteen-day period commencing October 16.
The government has been conducting a fortnightly review of export levies since March 27, in the backdrop of the conflict in West Asia. These are done based on the average international benchmark prices of crude oil, petrol, diesel and ATF observed since the previous review.
This is to ensure the domestic availability of retail fuels by disincentivising exports.

briefs.headline: Unemployment rate in country stands at 5% in September, stable compared to August: NSO
briefs.deck: The rural unemployment rate remains “broadly stable” at 4.2% against 4.1% in August, while urban rate marginally rises from 6.8% in August to 6.9% in this month
briefs.bodyText:
The Unemployment Rate (UR) in the country stood at 5% in September, stable compared to August, according to the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) conducted by the National Statistics Office (NSO). The Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation said here in a release on Thursday that the rural UR remained “broadly stable” at 4.2%, against 4.1% in August, while urban UR marginally rose from 6.8% in August to 6.9% in this month. “Compared with September 2025, the overall UR declined by 0.2 percentage points and reached at 5% in September 2026. Rural UR declined by 0.4 percentage points, from 4.6% in September, 2025 to 4.2% in September 2026. UR in urban areas remained broadly stable from 6.8% in September 2025 to 6.9% in September 2026,” the Ministry said.
Among females, the overall UR remained at 5.2%, up from 5.1% in August. Rural female UR stood at 3.9%, which, according to the government, is its lowest level in 2026, while urban female UR rose marginally from 8.9% to 9.2%. The government said unemployment rates declined year-on-year for both genders. The PLFS is the primary source of data on labour force participation and employment and unemployment conditions. At the all-India level, the monthly estimates are based on information collected from 3,70,513 persons surveyed.
The overall Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR), for persons aged 15 years and above, remained at 55.5% in September, compared to 55.6% in August. “In rural areas, LFPR was recorded at 58% against 58.2% in August 2026, while the urban LFPR registered a moderate increase of 0.3 percentage points, rising from 50.4% in August, 2026 to 50.7% in September 2026,” the Ministry said. Compared to September 2025, the overall LFPR increased by 0.2 percentage points, from 55.3% to 55.5%. The rural LFPR increased by 0.6 percentage points in one year, from 57.4% to 58%, while urban LFPR registered a marginal decline of 0.2 percentage points, from 50.9% to 50.7%. Overall female LFPR stood at 34.6% in September 2026, compared with 34.8% in August 2026. “Urban female LFPR recorded a notable month-on-month increase of 0.5 percentage points, rising from 25.4% to 25.9% and reaching its highest level since October 2025. Rural female LFPR estimated at 38.9% in September 2026 against 39.4% in the previous month,” the release added. Overall female LFPR increased by 0.5 percentage points, from 34.1% in September 2025 to 34.6% in September 2026.
The overall Worker Population Ratio (WPR) remained at 52.7% in September 2026, compared with 52.8% in August 2026. Overall WPR increased by 0.3 percentage points, from 52.4% in September 2025 to 52.7% in September 2026.
